description: **A mark upstream cannot place is bounded at zero, and the corner it cannot place is lost from the union rather than spreading through it.** Two lines do it, and this engine had neither. `rule.js` opens its bound with `x1 = item.x || 0, y1 = item.y || 0` — a `NaN` is *falsey* in JavaScript, so the first corner of an unplaceable mark bounds at the origin — while the second corner is taken with `item.x2 != null ? item.x2 : x1`, and a `NaN` is not `null`, so it keeps its `NaN`. Then `Bounds.union` is four bare comparisons — `if (b.x1 < this.x1) this.x1 = b.x1` and three more — every one of which is **false** against a `NaN`, so the unplaceable corner never replaces the edge already there. The surface that comes out is the size of everything the chart *could* place. This engine used `min` and `max` at both sites, and NaN-propagating ones do not: one `NaN` anywhere turned the whole surface into `NaN`. A scale with an empty range is the shortest way to a chart full of them — `scale(x)` has nothing to interpolate, so every tick and every label of the axis over it is unplaceable — and the axis still draws, still generates its ticks from the **domain**, and still lays out its labels, which is why upstream's surface here is the same 241 by 152 it would be with a working range. The `two` axis is the control: it places everything, and the bottom of the drawing is measured against it.
